newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat condemns U.S. Security Council veto.
newsitem.headline: Arafat condemns U.S. Security Council veto.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat condemned on Saturday a United States veto of a Security Council resolution calling on Israel to abandon plans to build a Jewish neighbourhood in mostly Arab East Jerusalem.
"It's a completely wrong decision," Arafat said after talks in Gaza with Jordanian Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti.
The U.S. used its veto on Friday to kill the resolution, supported by the 14 other Security Council members.
U.S. ambassador Bill Richardson said the council was ... "not an appropriate forum for debating the issues now under negotiation between the parties."

The veto followed a council debate in which virtually all of the nearly 50 speakers condemned Israel's plan to build 6,500 homes for Jews at a site called Har Homa by Israel and Jabal Abu Ghneim by the Palestinians.
Kabariti called for a ... "new American effort to prove that this veto does not mean some kind of backtracking from the original American position."
Kabariti said he conveyed a message of support for the Palestinians from King Hussein, who Arafat will meet later on Saturday in Jordan.
Arafat said he will also consult with King Hussein on a unilateral Israeli decision on Friday to hand over only nine percent more of the West Bank in the first of three pullbacks.
Arafat called the decision "a trick and conspiracy", saying their peace deal called for the transfer of 30 percent of West Bank territory in each of the pullbacks.
"I want to consult him (King Hussein) and to ask for his assistance to overcome the difficulties we are facing by the Israelis, including settlement in Jerusalem," Arafat said.
Israel regards the entire city of Jerusalem as its capital while the Palestinians see East Jerusalem as the captial of a future Palestinian state.
Israel welcomed the U.S. veto but slammed the European states that drafted the resolution, calling it "one-sided".

"We view gravely the European initiative which is unbalanced and one-sided and contrary to the position of the other members of the Security Council." said Israeli Foreign Ministry official Freddy Eytan.
During Kabariti's visit to Gaza with six other Jordanian ministers agreements were signed with the Palestinian Authority in the fields of public works and education.
"By these agreements we want to have the symbol of the relationship between the two states," Kabariti said.
